walkthroughs.body_html: Drive Theory argues that as arousal rises, performance rises linearly — provided the dominant response is well-learned. Beginners suffer because their dominant response may be incorrect. The Inverted U is a more popular GCSE model.

Introverts often prefer individual, fine-skill sports like archery, golf or long-distance running. Extroverts often thrive in team sports needing fast, gross skills like rugby or basketball. These are tendencies, not rules.

Athletes use mental rehearsal to picture the perfect skill, deep breathing to lower heart rate and positive self-talk to maintain confidence. These reduce anxiety and bring arousal toward the optimal zone.
